findings.disposition: exempted: the headroom is the annotation guard this script needs on any run of this measurement that does record a flip, and the figure is regenerated per run, so removing the padding would clip a label on the run that has one.
findings.evidence: plot.py lines 79-92; measured on image-0.png: series bbox y 179-561, x-axis spine at row 597, axes top near row 39, so about 140 px of the 558 px axes height (25 percent) sits above the highest datum.
findings.summary: The vertical limit is set to thirty times the largest residual (ax.set_ylim from min/3 to max*30), which reserves headroom for the flip annotations line 79 places 24 pt above a point. In this figure no decision flips, so no annotation is drawn and about a quarter of the panel above the highest datum is empty: the highest point sits at row 179 of an axes whose bottom spine is at row 597, and the only mark in that band is the 10^-1 tick label. A reader sees a plot that looks like it is waiting for a label that never comes, and the curve is compressed into the lower three quarters of the panel for no reason the picture shows. It does not block reading; the shape and the axis scales remain correct.

findings.disposition: exempted: the caption states the substitution, and the alternative (dropping the row would lose the zero-perturbation baseline the fixed-state claim is relative to).
findings.evidence: plot.py lines 61 and 93; image-0.png carries the six x tick labels 0, 10^-12, 10^-10, 10^-8, 10^-6, 10^-4, and the leftmost marker sits at x=212, inside the log axis.
findings.summary: The x tick for the zero-perturbation sample is labelled '0' while its datum is drawn at 1e-13 (line 61 substitutes 1e-13 for an epsilon of zero so the row can appear on a logarithmic axis). The figure alone therefore shows a point labelled 0 on an axis that cannot contain zero. The fragment's caption explains the substitution, so a reader of the page is served, but the image travels without that caption wherever a reader takes the picture alone, and this tick is the one place on the plot that states a value the axis cannot represent.

item_verdicts.caption_independence: The fragment's caption is not a repeat of the figure's identity: it names the fixed state, the sixteen lanes and the device, explains the 1e-13 placement of the zero row, and states the no-flip result an unlabelled curve cannot show by itself. No caption finding is raised.

Neither stops the figure carrying the claim its evidence record rests on: the fixed-state residual is continuous in the drive across 0 to 1e-4.

rubric_lines: RUBRIC legibility: pass. One blue line with six markers on logarithmic axes, titled 'drive perturbation' and 'fresh residual norm', with power-of-ten y ticks and x ticks reading 0, 10^-12, 10^-10, 10^-8, 10^-6, 10^-4. The rise from a floor near 1e-6 to about 1.8e-2 is visible at a glance and the flat-then-steepening shape reads without zooming.

The one dilution is the roughly quarter of the axes height left blank above the highest datum, recorded as finding 1; it is headroom reserved for flip annotations this figure has none of, not decoration.

RUBRIC decoration: pass. No gridlines, no background fill, no band or shading, no gradient, no drop shadow and no title. The top and right spines are absent, only the left and bottom axes carry a scale, and the minor tick marks on both are the only other furniture.

RUBRIC table_form: pass. The artifact is one continuous relationship, residual norm against additive drive perturbation, whose shape is the claim: a flat floor, then a rising branch. The six rows already appear as a table in the evidence fragment; the plot is what makes the continuity visible, so the image is not a picture of a table.

RUBRIC label_collision: pass. No text is clipped: the ink bounding box is (95,56)-(1344,656) inside a 1399x720 canvas and the outer 2 px frame carries zero non-white pixels. No text artist overlaps another, none sits over the line, and there are no direct labels at all because the drawing script annotates only where a membership, cut-set, normal-form, fragment, topology, qualification or X-point decision flips, and the reviewed measurement records zero flips at every epsilon.
